quarterly_data.signal: CFO Sooncheol Park: new highs in Q2 for both revenue and operating profit, building on the record Q1. Total revenue 171.5 trillion won (+28% QoQ); operating profit 89.5 trillion won (+56% QoQ); operating margin 52% vs 43% in Q1; net profit 71.6 trillion won (+52% QoQ); EPS 10,849 won for common and preferred (+52%); R&D expense a quarterly high of 16 trillion won vs 11 trillion won in Q1. The stronger US dollar added around 3.1 trillion won to operating profit QoQ, mainly in the component businesses. DS: DRAM and NAND bit shipments at all-time highs; System LSI faced mobile headwinds; Foundry gained from higher utilization and demand for all advanced nodes. DX: YoY revenue growth on premium and AI products, but operating profit declined as rising component costs lowered profitability. MX revenue 32.3 trillion won with MX + Network combined operating profit turning to a loss of 0.7 trillion won. Q2 includes a cumulative H1 accrual for a special performance incentive equal to around 10.5% of cumulative H1 operating profit (none was accrued in Q1); part of it was capitalised into work-in-progress inventory and will be expensed as that inventory is sold from Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue KRW 171.5 trillion (+28% QoQ); operating profit KRW 89.5 trillion (+56% QoQ, 52% margin); net profit KRW 71.6 trillion; R&D KRW 16 trillion; FX +KRW 3.1 trillion; incentive accrual ~10.5% of H1 operating profit

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 capex 16.8 trillion won, up 5.5 trillion won QoQ: DS Division 15.4 trillion won, Display 0.7 trillion won. Memory capex rose QoQ as Samsung expanded investment in the new fab in Pyeongtaek and other infrastructure on expectations of continued strong AI demand, plus advanced R&D. Foundry capex also rose QoQ as investment accelerated to support the Taylor fab ramp-up in the US, which remains on track. Display capex rose on supplementary investment in the Gen 8.6 line. CFO: the DS Division will keep strengthening core technology through optimized capex and proactive R&D investment.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capex KRW 16.8 trillion (+KRW 5.5 trillion QoQ); DS KRW 15.4 trillion; Display KRW 0.7 trillion

quarterly_data.signal: Memory supply-demand view (Memory EVP Jaejune Kim): with Agentic AI spreading, token consumption has grown exponentially, driving an unprecedented rise in demand for AI servers and general computing servers; AI frontier model developers short of hyperscaler cloud capacity are turning to neocloud providers, which have become major buyers from server OEMs, and frontier model developers are increasingly approaching Samsung directly to secure memory, sharing mid-to-long-term forecasts and requesting multi-year supply agreements. Mobile/PC demand is moderating as customers raise end-product prices, but additional demand for server DRAM, SSDs and HBM is far exceeding it, so the supply-demand gap next year 'will become much wider'; customers' demand is outgrowing supply despite production increases, and DRAM and NAND product mix will be optimised pre-emptively. With the lead time from new fab construction to wafer output exceeding three and a half years, management believes a significant increase in incremental supply is unlikely through 2028: unmet 2026 demand is likely to carry over, constraints are expected to be even more severe in 2027 than in 2026, and the shortage is expected to persist through 2028 (limited visibility beyond 2029). Capacity approach: clean-room capacity first through pre-emptive investment, then equipment installed flexibly with demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Memory shortage expected to persist through 2028; 2027 tighter than 2026; fab lead time over three and a half years

quarterly_data.signal: Memory multi-year supply contracts (Memory EVP Jaejune Kim): Samsung signs multi-year supply agreements on a five-year term, renegotiated annually with an option to add one more year (rolling basis). Agreements are already finalized with the top five global data center customers, and talks with five additional major accounts are in the final stages; almost all major customers want long-term supply, and existing contract holders are seeking additional volume. Samsung plans to allocate approximately 60% to 70% of total capacity to long-term contracts, keeping capacity for customers without multi-year contracts, and expects DRAM and NAND volumes under multi-year contracts to 'easily account for 60% to 70%' of planned capacity once pending contracts close. Priority goes to customers accepting mutually binding terms with committed demand. The contracts require substantial advance payments maintained over the contract period; Samsung has already received one-fourth of these payments and expects the balance to grow (further detail under NDA). Pricing is differentiated by customer segment and product, with minimum price floors set for conventional products to cover future investment risk; Samsung says it keeps a balanced customer portfolio without over-reliance on any single customer. CFO: customer prepayments on memory LTAs may affect free cash flow.
quarterly_data.figure: 5-year rolling LTAs signed with top five global data center customers; five more in final talks; 60% to 70% of capacity under LTAs; one-fourth of advance payments received; price floors on conventional products

quarterly_data.signal: Memory Q2 results and Q3 outlook (Memory EVP Jaejune Kim): Q2 DRAM bit shipments rose by the low teens percentage QoQ, exceeding guidance; NAND bit shipments rose by a low-single-digit percentage, in line with guidance. Q2 ASP rose by mid 40% for DRAM and high 60% for NAND QoQ. Record-high bit shipments for both DRAM and NAND and an all-time-high server share of bit sales; memory set another quarterly record. Q3 outlook: with DRAM and NAND inventories significantly low, QoQ bit growth is expected in the mid-single digits for DRAM and high-single digits for NAND. CFO: DS growth continues in H2 on Agentic AI demand, with expanded sales of HBM4 including HBM4E, DDR5, SOCAMM2 and eSSD.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 DRAM bits +low teens % QoQ, NAND +low single digit %; DRAM ASP +mid 40%, NAND ASP +high 60% QoQ; Q3 bit growth DRAM mid-single digits, NAND high-single digits

quarterly_data.signal: System LSI and set businesses (Q2 call): System LSI (EVP Jason Shin) held quarterly revenue despite flagship seasonality and a weak Chinese mobile market, achieving record-high H1 revenue; it secured a next-generation flagship SoC contract (development and production on plan) and new awards from major customers in SoC, image sensor and LSI products, is developing Custom SoC opportunities using its design, foundry, memory and packaging capabilities, strengthening 200-megapixel sensors, high-end DDI and growing Power ICs. Samsung Display began mass production at its Gen 8.6 IT OLED line in July; initial fixed costs are expected to weigh on short-term earnings, and Display sales volume may decline on higher set prices caused by memory supply constraints. MX expects annual smartphone shipments to decline on soft demand and rising memory prices (premium resilient; full-year sales value and ASP expected to rise), with the mobile memory cost burden continuing through H2; Intelligent Eyewear launches later this year. Harman acquired ZF's ADAS business (smart camera sensors, high-performance controllers) and Sound United. Robotics: a new RX Business Office reporting to the CEO, a robotics pilot production line and data factory being built in Gumi, targeting B2B manufacturing/logistics humanoid robots first.
quarterly_data.figure: System LSI record H1 revenue; Gen 8.6 IT OLED mass production from July 2026; smartphone shipments expected to decline in 2026

players.product: leading-edge wafer fab (SF3/SF2 GAA logic dies)

quarterly_data.signal: Foundry (EVP Sukchae Kang): Q2 revenue increased on growing demand for memory HBM base-die products and products for US customers; earnings improved significantly before incentive-related charges. The 2nm order pipeline keeps expanding around major HPC customers including cloud service providers: in Q2 Samsung secured 2nm projects from major CSPs and AI/HPC customers, now in the design phase, and is in talks with Broadcom and other major customers on other projects; 2nm project wins are expected to more than double YoY in 2026. H2 2026: mass production of new mobile products on 2nd-generation 2nm, volume ramp of LPU products for major 4nm customers, and scaling of memory base-die sales; with growth at key US and China customers across all nodes, Samsung expects double-digit or higher YoY foundry revenue growth. Advanced nodes are projected to exceed 50% of revenue and AI/HPC applications to rise from the high-teens percentage in 2025 to over 30% in 2026. Utilization improved YoY at all nodes, with advanced nodes (8nm and below) at full utilization; 2nd-generation 2nm ramps in H2 after successful 1st-generation mass production, with yields expected to stabilise. Management expects significant YoY profitability improvement from utilization, yields and pricing adjustments and believes a turnaround is 'possible in the near-term', though timing is hard to predict.
quarterly_data.figure: 2nm project wins expected to more than double YoY in 2026; foundry revenue growth double-digit or higher YoY; advanced nodes over 50% of revenue; AI/HPC from high-teens % (2025) to over 30% (2026); 8nm and below at full utilization

quarterly_data.signal: Foundry capacity plan (EVP Sukchae Kang): with demand outpacing advanced-node capacity, Samsung is expanding it. Taylor Fab 1 is preparing to start operations by 2026 as planned and will gradually ramp 2nm capacity; Taylor Fab 2 will begin construction by the end of this year, targeting mass production by 2030. Customer inquiries for 1.4nm are increasing and Samsung is reviewing options to secure additional fab capacity, to be planned in phases with customer engagements. Mature nodes shift toward higher-value specialty applications: capacity is being expanded in 8nm, 17nm, CIS and eNVM, while capacity is secured for next-generation technologies such as ISC and silicon photonics. Q2 foundry capex rose QoQ as investment accelerated for the Taylor ramp-up.
quarterly_data.figure: Taylor Fab 1 operations by 2026 (2nm ramp); Taylor Fab 2 construction by end-2026, mass production by 2030; 1.4nm inquiries rising

quarterly_data.signal: HBM (Memory EVP Jaejune Kim): Samsung expanded HBM4 supply in Q2 and shipped the industry's first HBM4E samples to major customers (company claim). Customer qualifications for individual HBM4 projects are 'coming to an end smoothly', and demand is rising rapidly with customers' H2 project ramps; 1c-nano capacity expansion and yield improvement are progressing as planned, expanding HBM supply capacity. Samsung expects HBM4 sales to rise more than threefold QoQ in Q3 and HBM4 to account for well over 60% of HBM revenue in H2, and expects H2 HBM market share broadly in line with its overall DRAM market share. For 2027, HBM supply agreements are already signed with customers, and Samsung believes HBM4E is competitive enough to commercialize with major customers as planned. Samsung keeps a balanced HBM / conventional DRAM supply mix regardless of the profitability difference, watching the relative growth of HBM and server DRAM demand.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM4 sales expected to rise more than threefold QoQ in Q3; HBM4 well over 60% of H2 HBM revenue; 2027 HBM supply agreements signed

players.product: PM1743/PM9D3a E3.S & U.2 enterprise PCIe Gen5 SSD

quarterly_data.signal: NAND / server SSD (Memory EVP Jaejune Kim): with Agentic AI, server SSD demand is growing across general-purpose computing servers and dedicated KV-cache storage servers, and NAND made a significant contribution to Q2 memory results. Server SSD is expected to exceed 60% of Samsung's NAND sales mix this year, up more than 20 percentage points YoY. Samsung is engaging major customers on multi-year NAND agreements. PCIe Gen 6 SSDs are receiving positive feedback from major customers and Samsung expects to lead the early Gen 6 AI-platform market. After completing V9 2-terabit QLC in March, the lineup now includes 256-terabyte server SSDs, and H2 QLC bit shipments are expected to more than double versus H1. V10 BV NAND (bonding, three-stack architecture) is scheduled for mass production in August 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Server SSD over 60% of 2026 NAND sales mix (+20pp+ YoY); H2 QLC bits more than double H1; V10 BV NAND mass production August
